document_title: Texas comptroller proposes that AI and cloud computing fall outside the data processing tax
_note: Caption carried verbatim from caption.txt. Slide strings polished by the copywriter from storyboard.md and held to the claim quotes in claims.json. Every numeral is in claims.json or figures.json. Drawn to illustrate appears only on S3. Every dollar figure is the comptroller's own estimate of a proposed rule. The rule is proposed and never adopted.
caption:
Does Texas tax AI as data processing?

Comptroller Don Huffines says the Legislature never taxed AI. His proposed Rule 3.308 amendments would class cloud, AI and quantum computing as hosted technology services, outside the tax.

The release says it saves Texans money. His fiscal note has the state losing $1,947,310,000 in fiscal 2027 and $4,286,040,000 in 2032. It has local governments losing $507,450,000 in 2027 and $1,116,890,000 in 2032. The note calls the economic effect "insignificant".

Nothing is adopted yet. Comments to Robin Robinson must arrive by December 20th, the earliest adoption date.

The deck stacks the estimate, one sheet per million dollars.

Comptroller-elect Sarah Eckhardt takes over January 1st. She asked him to halt rule changes begun since August 1st. Does this one survive the handover?

#TexasComptroller #SalesTax #TexasRegister

S1.headline: Texas may stop taxing AI as data processing
S1.body: On November 18th Comptroller Don Huffines announced a proposal to count cloud computing and AI as hosted technology services, outside the tax on data processing. His office estimates the state's loss at $1,947,310,000 in fiscal year 2027.
strings: Texas may stop taxing AI as data processing

On November 18th Comptroller Don Huffines announced a proposal to count cloud computing and AI as hosted technology services, outside the tax on data processing. His office estimates the state's loss at $1,947,310,000 in fiscal year 2027.

S2.headline: Customer data in, organized data back
S2.body: Huffines says the Legislature taxed data processing in 1987. The proposal defines the service as a provider processing data the customer supplied and returning it in an organized and usable format the customer asked for.
strings: Customer data in, organized data back

Huffines says the Legislature taxed data processing in 1987. The proposal defines the service as a provider processing data the customer supplied and returning it in an organized and usable format the customer asked for.

S3.headline: Using a provider's computing would not count
S3.body: A customer using a provider's software, platform or computing resources on its own data would not be a data processing service. Storing or manipulating data alone would not count either. The hall is drawn to illustrate.
strings: Using a provider's computing would not count

A customer using a provider's software, platform or computing resources on its own data would not be a data processing service. Storing or manipulating data alone would not count either. The hall is drawn to illustrate.

S4.headline: Cloud, AI and quantum, named in the proposal
S4.body: The proposal defines hosted technology services to include cloud computing, artificial intelligence and quantum computing. It says hosted technology services are not data processing and are not taxable.
strings: Cloud, AI and quantum, named in the proposal

The proposal defines hosted technology services to include cloud computing, artificial intelligence and quantum computing. It says hosted technology services are not data processing and are not taxable.

S5.headline: Estimated state loss hits $4.3 billion by 2032
S5.body: The comptroller's estimate of the state's loss rises in each year it counts, from $1,947,310,000 in fiscal year 2027 to $4,286,040,000 in 2032. Each sheet of paper here stands for one million dollars of it.
strings: Estimated state loss hits $4.3 billion by 2032

The comptroller's estimate of the state's loss rises in each year it counts, from $1,947,310,000 in fiscal year 2027 to $4,286,040,000 in 2032. Each sheet of paper here stands for one million dollars of it.

S6.headline: Cities, counties and transit would lose too
S6.body: The same note estimates that local governments would lose $507,450,000 in fiscal year 2027 and $1,116,890,000 in 2032. Cities, counties and transit authorities are among them.
strings: Cities, counties and transit would lose too
The same note estimates that local governments would lose $507,450,000 in fiscal year 2027 and $1,116,890,000 in 2032. Cities, counties and transit authorities are among them.

S7.headline: "Insignificant effect on this state's economy"
S7.body: That is the chief revenue estimator's finding. It sits in the same note that estimates the losses. The note also says a likely negative effect on sales tax remittances can't be estimated.
strings: That is the chief revenue estimator's finding. It sits in the same note that estimates the losses. The note also says a likely negative effect on sales tax remittances can't be estimated.

S8.headline: Comments close December 20th
S8.body: The proposal ran in the Texas Register on November 20th. The comptroller must receive comments within 30 days. The earliest possible adoption date is December 20th.
strings: The proposal ran in the Texas Register on November 20th. The comptroller must receive comments within 30 days. The earliest possible adoption date is December 20th.

S9.headline: It is still only a proposal
S9.body: Mail or email comments to Robin Robinson, Associate Deputy Comptroller for Tax. The address is Robin.Robinson@cpa.texas.gov. Comments must arrive by December 20th.
